evals.prompt: Our notes app sells a Pro lifetime unlock + monthly sub via StoreKit 2. We're getting a bunch of 1-star reviews from users in China saying Pro vanished after they "switched region" and Restore Purchases does nothing. Many of them bought on a US Apple ID because we only launched in the US, then switched back to their CN account. Here's our store code: evals/storekit-account-switch-entitlements/files/StoreManager.swift. What's going on and how do we fix it? Give me a concrete plan and the code changes.
evals.expected_output: Explains purchases belong to the paying Apple Account (case B: different account), that AppStore.sync only syncs current account; flags the Storefront.updates clearing bug; proposes a bounded on-device retention (keychain snapshot, bounded window from last owner verification, revocation/family-sharing exclusions) or server accounts as alternative; gives code changes and user-facing copy telling users to switch back.
assertions: Identifies that purchases belong to the paying Apple Account and that switching to a different account (not the storefront) is the cause
States that Restore Purchases / AppStore.sync only syncs the currently signed-in account, so it cannot fix this
Flags that the Storefront.updates handler clearing isPro is a bug
Proposes a time-bounded retention window (not a permanent flag) as the fix or a main option
Specifies that only a fresh verification on the paying account refreshes/extends the window
Excludes or immediately locks on revoked/refunded transactions (and notes currentEntitlements omits revoked, so latest(for:) or equivalent is needed)
Excludes family-shared transactions from retention
Stores the snapshot in the Keychain (not UserDefaults), device-only / not iCloud-synced
Includes user-facing copy telling users to switch back to the purchasing Apple Account
Provides concrete Swift code changes

evals.prompt: quick design q for my iOS app (StoreKit 2, one non-consumable 'Pro'). some users switch between their HK and CN apple accounts and lose Pro. simplest fix I can think of is: once we've ever seen a verified Pro transaction, set a keychain flag hasPro=true forever and trust it. any problems with that? what would you do instead? keep it short-ish.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: permanent flag means refunds never revoke, family-sharing leaks, unbounded; recommends bounded retention window refreshed only by owner-account verification, revocation wins, clear UI copy to switch back, keychain unreadable != absent; mentions server account alternative briefly.
assertions: Says a permanent hasPro flag means refunds/revocations never take effect
Mentions family sharing risk (access via organizer that can end) or ownership-type check
Recommends a bounded time window instead of forever
Says the window is refreshed only by re-verification on the paying account
Recommends telling users to switch back to the purchasing account (and not relying on Restore)
Mentions Keychain read failures (locked device/background) must not be treated as absent, or keychain accessibility/iCloud sync considerations
Stays reasonably short (under ~600 words)
